answer: Attackers face a real cost per fake account, so swarming the oasis of honest agents with clones becomes expensive. One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Reputation flows like a river, carrying weight only from verified stake, while a ridge of peer attestations blocks unbacked newcomers from voting. Mass registration collapses under cumulative slashing risk, making sybil farming economically irrational. In practice, Agent0040 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
